name: TB-500

lead: TB-500 is the name used by research-peptide vendors for a synthetic version of thymosin beta-4 (Tβ4) or a fragment of it; the exact molecule sold varies by supplier. Tβ4 itself is a 43-amino-acid protein that is abundant in most human cells and binds actin.

In recovery and looksmaxxing communities it is marketed for tendon, muscle and skin repair, often stacked with BPC-157. The legitimate research on full-length Tβ4 involves wound, eye and cardiac repair, and evidence that vendor TB-500 products do the same in healthy people is essentially absent.

paras: Tβ4 sequesters monomeric actin, which influences cell migration, and in animal models it has been linked to angiogenesis, reduced inflammation and improved cell survival in injured tissue. Whether the shorter fragment sold as TB-500 reproduces these effects is not well established.

Human safety data for the vendor products are lacking, and product identity and purity are inconsistent. Pro-angiogenic activity raises a theoretical concern in people with cancer risk. TB-500 is not an approved drug and is banned by WADA, and a high-profile Australian sports supplement scandal involved thymosin beta-4.
